reported.title: Relay pulse length and start timing wrong
reported.description: The run is scheduled from the moment startRun() executes (line 30 sets nextRunAt = now + CYCLE_MS), and stopRunAt is computed from that same now (line 29), but the loop only checks `now >= stopRunAt` (line 64) and `now >= nextRunAt` (line 69) with 16-bit millis() values (line 16), so the pulse is cut short and runs drift. Measured evidence shows pulses lasting 201 ms and 500 ms instead of 2000 ± 150 ms, and D6 missing 10 of 13 triggers. The 16-bit wrap in tickNow() also breaks the comparisons, so the first run does not reliably start 5000 ms after power-up. D6 missed 10 of 13 trigger(s): D6 did not start within 100 ms of the trigger at 952 ms. 8 of 8 pulse(s) had the wrong length: pulse from 5.00 s lasted 201 ms, expected 2000 ± 150 ms.

reported.title: Serial 'mix <n>' not printed once per 5000 ms
reported.description: announceRun() is only called from startRun() (line 31), which is gated by the 16-bit wrap-prone comparison at line 69 and by nextRunAt being reset to now + CYCLE_MS at line 30 rather than a fixed schedule. Measured evidence shows 98 of 100 intervals out of tolerance with gaps of 2001 ms, 2000 ms and 8 ms, and one scenario with no matching line at all in 4.65 s. The schedule therefore does not hold the required 5000 ± 250 ms period. Expected /^mix [0-9]+$/ every 5000 ± 250 ms; 98 of 100 intervals were out of tolerance, worst gap 4927 ms.

reported.title: Relay toggles more than twice per 5000 ms window
reported.description: drive() (lines 46-47) recomputes the relay state from `running && !held()` on every loop pass with no debounce or edge latching, so each bounce or chatter on D3 toggles D6 immediately. Measured evidence shows 16, 22 and 7 toggles in a 5000 ms window against a limit of 2. The lack of any hysteresis or minimum-state-time in drive() lets contact bounce propagate straight to the relay. D6 toggled 16 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 5.00 s (limit 2), and 16 times over the whole 8.00 s run.

truth.description: The 16-bit clock is compared with absolute deadlines, so the schedule breaks whenever the clock wraps, every 65.5 s of uptime

judge_input.spec:
- Mixer relay on D6; hold switch on D3 with internal pull-up (active LOW).
- Run the mixer (D6 HIGH) for 2000 ms out of every 5000 ms, the first run starting 5000 ms after power-up.
- Print `mix <n>` when each run starts, once per 5000 ms ±250 ms.
- While D3 is held LOW, keep D6 LOW. The runs are still counted and printed.
- The mixer must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
